Update from runtime team and quick remediation we applied:

Root cause (summary): a recent change to the burst-aware batching heuristic (commit 9d3a7b) made the runtime over-eagerly consolidate in-flight requests into larger micro-batches when client pacing patterns were highly variable. That optimization reduced throughput under normal conditions but introduced occasional token-drain pauses for certain stream sessions when clients emitted small, frequent bursts. The effect amplified for sessions going through a particular edge shard in us-west-2 due to a skewed sequence-length distribution.

Immediate actions taken (Aug 10 10:48 PDT):
- Rolled back the batching heuristic toggle to conservative mode (hotfix revert of 9d3a7b).
- Increased KV cache retention for shard us-west-2 to 2x to reduce miss amplification.
- Deployed a telemetry patch that logs per-stream token-emit latency and includes a short trace (attached).

Observed result: within 20–30 minutes of the rollback, FinTrio reported chunk delivery stabilized; median chunk latency for affected sessions dropped from ~7s to ~0.5s in our internal sampling.

Artifacts attached: livepipe-trace.log (excerpted trace for req-7f12b3a4), incident-timeline.csv (timeline of deploys + mitigations).

Next steps:
- We'll run a controlled A/B test of a revised batching algorithm that includes a per-client pacing threshold guard. Target ETA for safe rollout: 2027-08-16.
- Postmortem write-up due by Aug 13; include blameless timeline, RCA, corrective actions, and customer-facing remediation docs.
- Offer FinTrio a one-time usage credit for affected premium sessions (TBD by Sales).

-Marissa (runtime lead)

Subject: Post-incident brief — LivePipe streaming latency (Aug 9–11)

Alice — thank you again for your patience and collaboration while we investigated the LivePipe streaming latency you reported. Below is a concise customer-facing summary and recommended mitigations you can keep in place while we complete the postmortem.

What happened (short summary):
- On Aug 9 we observed intermittent 6–12s pauses for chunked streaming deliveries affecting a subset of sessions routed through an edge shard in us-west-2. The underlying cause was an overly aggressive batching heuristic introduced in a performance change (commit 9d3a7b) that, under certain client pacing patterns, deferred token emission while trying to form larger micro-batches.

Impact:
- FinTrio: ~14% error spike for premium chat flows during the incident window; customer ops temporarily diverted traffic to a secondary endpoint.
- Scope: localized to a narrow subset of edge shard traffic and sequence-length distributions; not a global outage.

What we did:
- Aug 10 10:48 PDT: rolled back batching heuristic to conservative defaults and increased KV cache retention for impacted shard.
- Deployed additional telemetry and captured traces (attached).
- Verified chunk delivery latency returned to baseline within ~30 minutes for sampled sessions.

Short-term mitigations for your side (recommended until Aug 16 rollout):
- Set client header X-RW-Stream-Fallback: true so stalled streams use fallback polling.
- Reduce client max_chunk_size to 4kB for sensitive live flows during high concurrency windows.
- Add a 50–100ms jitter to client token emission when sending bursts to avoid pathological pacing alignments.

What to expect next:
- We will perform an internal A/B test of a revised batching algorithm with a per-client pacing gate and release to a subset of traffic on Aug 16.
- A full, blameless postmortem will be delivered by Aug 13 that contains a timeline, RCA, and long-term corrective actions.
- Sales will follow up on a proposed credit for impacted premium sessions — Ben from Sales (cc'd) will coordinate.

Attachments included: livepipe-trace.log (excerpt), incident-timeline.csv

If you want a short tech-ops call tomorrow to walk through the artifacts and mitigation steps we can set aside 30 minutes — propose 10:00 or 14:00 PDT.

Apologies again for the disruption — we appreciate you working with us on the verification.

Best,
